content.title: About
content.content: Iced brewed green tea unsweetened is a refreshing beverage made from Camellia sinensis leaves that undergo a cold‑water extraction. It retains the light, vegetal aroma of green tea while being served chilled and without any added sweeteners.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green tea is rich in polyphenols, especially catechins, which have strong antioxidant properties.
Cold brewing preserves more vitamin C than hot brewing because the lower temperature does not degrade it.
In Japan, cold green tea (mucha) is traditionally served during summer to cool the body.
Without sugar, the drink is very low in calories – about 0‑2 kcal per 100 ml.
Leaves used for cold brew are often younger, giving the tea a milder flavor.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Catechins help neutralize free radicals, supporting cellular health.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Regular consumption of green tea may help lower LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Metabolism boost
items.content: Caffeine and L‑theanine can increase metabolic rate and aid fat oxidation.

items.title: Sugar‑free hydration
items.content: Provides fluid without added calories, making it ideal for hydration.

items.title: Cognitive enhancement
items.content: The combination of caffeine and L‑theanine improves focus and alertness.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience jitteriness, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Green tea can amplify the effects of anticoagulants and certain antidepressants.

items.title: Iron absorption
items.content: Tannins may reduce iron absorption, so people with anemia should drink tea between meals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the iced unsweetened green tea on its own, or add a slice of lemon, mint, or ginger for extra flavor. It works well in cocktails, smoothies, or as a base for marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared beverage in a sealed bottle in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Flavor may diminish with prolonged storage.
